contract: skills-package/v3 — the signature covers the schema
note: `config_schema` lives in `skill.yaml`, so the manifest signature already covers it. These cases prove that placement is load-bearing rather than incidental: a schema an intermediary can widen is a schema that decides nothing.
refusal_note: Each case gives the manifest as signed and the manifest as presented. A conforming loader signs and verifies the canonicalised `skill.yaml`, so any difference between the two is a verification failure — raising SkillSecurityError, not a validation error.
ordering_note: The mutations here are deliberately grammar-valid. An invalid one may be refused by schema validation before verification is reached, which is also correct behaviour but proves nothing about whether the signature covers the schema.

cases.name: widened_bound_after_signing
cases.why: A widened bound is the mutation with a motive: it admits configuration the author never agreed to accept, and every value it newly admits is grammar-valid.

cases.name: added_key_after_signing
cases.why: An added key opens a surface the author closed by not declaring it.

cases.name: removed_schema_after_signing
cases.note: Removing the schema entirely is not a way to relax it — absence admits only an empty `config` — but it is still a difference from what was signed, and is refused as one rather than tolerated as harmless.

cases.name: default_changed_after_signing
cases.why: A default is the value the skill runs on when an operator writes nothing, so changing it changes behaviour without changing any document.
